sentences.text: Sanchiaosaurus dengi is the sole species of an extinct basal nothosauroid, a group of reptiles from the Middle Triassic of southwestern China.
This animal belongs to the class Reptilia and sits within the broader parent group Nothosauroidea.
The genus was first described by Yang Zhongjian in 1965 based on a single partial skeleton known as the holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on.
Its name combines the locality Sanchiao with the Greek word sauros, meaning lizard.
Fossils were found near Guiyang in the Guanling Formation, dating to the Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic, approximately 245 million years ago.
